title: product brief
description: product/brief.json — what the app is, who it is for, and what would make it work. `ship scout brief` answers whether a keyword is winnable; this answers whether there is a product behind it. The market half is computed from the scout brief and cannot be edited into something the storefront does not say; the product half is the agent's, and every claim in it cites a review theme.

^_.description: Annotation kept beside the data it explains. Ignored by every loader.

term.description: The keyword the scout brief was built on, kept so the two artifacts can be re-joined.

source.description: Path of the scout brief this was drafted from. Provenance, not an input: nothing re-reads it.

verdict.description: Copied from the scout brief. Computed, never authored — a `go` typed in by hand is the failure this whole artifact exists to prevent.

jobs.description: Jobs to be done, most important first. Each is a job a real reviewer described, not one the product would like to serve.

job.description: Phrased as the user's situation and desired outcome, not as a feature.

evidence.description: Theme labels from research/<slug>/themes.json backing this job. A job with no theme behind it is a guess wearing a citation's clothes.

items.description: A flow id from src/lib/flows.mjs. The closed vocabulary is the join key across research, ux.json, analytics events and QA.

context.description: When and where they reach for this. A brief that cannot name the moment cannot name the first screen.

notFor.description: Who this deliberately does not serve. The scope the roadmap may not quietly widen into.

valueProp.description: One sentence, in the user's words. If it does not survive being read aloud to a stranger it is not one.

northStar.description: The single action that means the product worked. One, not a dashboard.

flow.description: A flow id from src/lib/flows.mjs. The closed vocabulary is the join key across research, ux.json, analytics events and QA.

activation.description: The moment a new install becomes a user. `ship analytics diagnose` reads the activation stage against this.

event.description: A `<flow>_<verb>` event name, as `eventName()` in src/lib/flows.mjs builds it — so the app emits, the funnel counts and the brief names the same string.

within.description: How long a user has to reach it before they are lost. Not a target; the window the funnel is measured over.

retention.description: Why anyone opens it a second time. An app with no answer here is a one-session utility, which is a fine thing to be and an expensive thing to acquire for.

items.description: A flow id from src/lib/flows.mjs. The closed vocabulary is the join key across research, ux.json, analytics events and QA.

gate.description: What sits behind the paywall, in the user's terms. `free` and `undecided` leave this empty.

incumbentPrices.description: What the top-10 charge, read off the storefront. Computed; the drafted number is a fact about the market, not a decision.

risks.description: What would make this fail. The gate-derived ones are computed from the scout brief; an agent may add more but may not delete one.

source.description: `scout` risks are computed from the storefront and survive a re-draft; the others do not.
